title: ThinkPad's Unlikely AI Comeback
caption:
Remember the ThinkPad? That iconic black slab, once a corporate workhorse, is now quietly powering the next wave of AI development. For decades, its design ethos prioritized ruggedness and reliability over flash. But as the demands of local AI processing exploded, Lenovo's ThinkPads have undergone a subtle but significant transformation, evolving into some of the most capable mobile AI workstations available.

It's not just about raw CPU power anymore; it's about dedicated neural processing units, advanced GPUs, and optimized cooling systems packed into a familiar, no-nonsense chassis. This evolution proves that even the most established hardware can adapt and lead in a rapidly changing software-driven world, offering serious compute for serious builders.

Want to understand the hardware behind today's AI breakthroughs? BUILD for the field guide.

slides.title: The Bento Box Legacy
slides.body: IBM's original ThinkPad design prioritized durability, keyboard quality, and a distinct aesthetic. It became synonymous with reliability for professionals worldwide.

slides.definition: A personal computer, typically a laptop, optimized with high-performance GPUs, NPUs, and RAM for local AI model training and inference.
slides.example: Modern ThinkPads, like the P1 Gen 6, function as potent AI workstations.

slides.title: What Modern AI Demands
bullets: Dedicated Neural Processing Units (NPUs) for efficient on-device AI.
High-end discrete GPUs (NVIDIA, AMD) for parallel processing.
Large, fast RAM for handling massive datasets.
slides.footer: This isn't just about faster clock speeds anymore.
